content.title: HEALTHY-EATING {{MISTAKES}} HIDING IN YOUR KITCHEN
facts: **Salad Dressing** – Skipping oil entirely can mean less absorption of vitamin A, E, and K from your greens; a drizzle of healthy fat actually helps your body use them.
**Store-Bought Granola** – Many "healthy" granolas pack more added sugar per serving than people expect; the label matters more than the packaging.
**Smoothies** – Blending fruit breaks down its fiber structure, so a smoothie can raise blood sugar faster than eating the same fruit whole.
**Air Frying** – Using an air fryer doesn't automatically make a dish light if it still has the same oil and breading as deep frying.
**Canned Beans** – Rinsing them under water lowers the sodium content, a simple step most people skip.
**Meal Prep Containers** – Sealing hot food right away traps steam and can speed up spoilage; letting it cool a bit first helps it last longer.
**Frozen Vegetables** – Thawing them at room temperature before cooking often leaves them soggy and watery; cooking straight from frozen keeps texture and nutrients better.
**Flavored Yogurt** – Many "protein" yogurts contain as much sugar as dessert; plain yogurt with your own toppings is usually the smarter base.
**Quinoa** – Skipping the rinse before cooking leaves a bitter coating that people mistake for it "just tasting healthy."
**Avocado Toast** – Piling it on refined white bread cancels out a good chunk of the fiber benefit you're aiming for.
**Follow along** – for more everyday fixes to make your healthy meals actually work.
content.caption:
None of this means your healthy meal is ruined forever or that you're doing everything wrong — small tweaks add up, and everyone's body reacts a little differently to food and prep. Think of these as gentle upgrades, not strict rules to stress over.
